findings.title: Opt-in still permits OpenAI ciphertext recovery and later lineage stripping
findings.trigger: Trusted native API-key opt-in, passthrough=false, encrypted reasoning history, upstream HTTP 400 error.code=invalid_encrypted_content; or a matching stored session invalid-ciphertext digest. WS ingress also strips matching lineage independently of opt-in.
findings.impact: HTTP retries after deleting encrypted_content from provider-owned reasoning (all encrypted reasoning, not only a uniquely identified rejected item), records ciphertext digests, and later requests strip matching history. WS recovery/ingress has the same policy gap. Content and opaque metadata may survive, but encrypted_content does not. This contradicts the explicitly promised intact encrypted history.
findings.evidence: Patch guards initial normalizers and ID sanitizer only. Retry branch at 1121 has no preserveCompatibleReasoning guard; trim helper at request_body.go:428 deletes encrypted_content; pre-strip at 754 and WS ingress check lineage without account policy. These are inherited branches left reachable by this proposal, not newly introduced recovery code.
findings.minimal_remedy: For opted-in accounts, gate ciphertext mutation, lineage recording and lineage pre-stripping at every HTTP/WS boundary; surface the original upstream rejection instead. Keep default/OpenAI/OAuth recovery unchanged.
findings.acceptance_test: Use real Forward with existing transport recorder, opted-in encrypted history and a 400 invalid_encrypted_content response. Assert original error/no second upstream request and no lineage record; seed a matching digest and assert first outbound ciphertext unchanged. Exercise actual WS ingress/recovery preparation with the same state. Repeat with policy=false to retain existing recovery.

findings.title: Later image-tool preparation rounds opaque reasoning numbers
findings.trigger: Opted-in compatibleReasoningHistory plus tools=[{"type":"image_generation","format":"png"}] through actual WS compatibility preparation or HTTP passthrough.
findings.impact: The later map[string]any json.Unmarshal decodes opaque=9007199254740993 as float64; tool format migration forces json.Marshal and emits 9007199254740992. The policy sanitizer preserves raw history earlier, but this later branch corrupts it. Native WS and HTTP passthrough diverge from the ordinary HTTP UseNumber decode path.
findings.evidence: Predicate accepts the legacy format field; normalizeOpenAIResponsesImageGenerationTools migrates/deletes it and returns true; request_body.go:1540 then 1544 use ordinary Unmarshal/Marshal of the entire request. Existing added fixture already tests this integer but never includes a tool that activates this branch.
findings.minimal_remedy: Replace this whole-body json.Unmarshal with existing decodeOpenAIJSONUseNumber; prefer raw field edits if lexical replay fidelity is required. No dependency needed.
findings.acceptance_test: Call real normalizeOpenAIResponsesWebSocketCompatibilityBody and real Forward passthrough with the existing history plus legacy image format/compression; assert expected tool migration and exact opaque numeric Raw, reasoning/ciphertext/IDs/references and tool pairing. No mirrored normalization mock.
